release_choice.fix_surface: python-sdk v1.30.0 (tag commit 8c2fa6eabacde869d75568e33b9d466b58c2f512) src/mcp/server/streamable_http_manager.py:42,45,99,101: DEFAULT_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT = 30 * 60 and DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS = 10_000 become StreamableHTTPSessionManager's session_idle_timeout and max_sessions defaults. At v1.28.1 (tag commit 777b8d06710c140e3606b0d4598e2aa48546c266, the constructor at lines 65-74) session_idle_timeout defaults to None and max_sessions does not exist. Read by syntax tree from the two tags' files, not imported
release_choice.fix_commits: 92120b4b0f50385af096592d7cee932fc1d994e7 (#3426, the 1.x backport) is one of the five commits from v1.29.1 to v1.30.0; d2290ca3434731b68ea3e2270bc06a6e6575931b (#3395) is in v2.1.1 to v2.2.0 (tag commit 9972c21aa42054fb1450c5fc614761ed11847ec6)
release_choice.release_notes: v1.30.0 body lines 13-17: idle Streamable HTTP sessions expire after 30 minutes with nothing in flight, at most 10 000 sessions, a 503 beyond, both off with None (#3426); line 33: the two FastMCP settings; line 38: the #3426 entry. The same body lists three other changes: a redirect is followed only within the MCP endpoint's origin by streamable_http_client and sse_client (#3448, lines 7-11), the OAuth client checks the authorization server's issuer (#3431, lines 19-22), and two new DeprecationWarnings (lines 24-27). v1.29.0 (tag commit 98b7159cb89274964055d2c016e3360a551280d0) and v1.29.1 (b22271305c59dfc7910f1493faea78cb1d396e48) add request body limits and fix tool-name validation, the FastMCP settings model and recursive output schemas
release_choice.two_x_line: 2.2.0 also fixes the advisory, but fastmcp 3.2.0 requires mcp<2.0, so the 2.x line is outside the recipe's resolution

dependent_metadata.workspace_declarations: The SDK workspace at fcc102a declares no mcp requirement of its own; openhands-sdk requires fastmcp>=3.2.0,<4 (openhands-sdk/pyproject.toml:13)

install_check.fastmcp_client_smoke: fastmcp 3.2.0 Client listed and called the one tool of an in-process FastMCP server over the in-memory transport (the installed wheel's fastmcp/client/transports/memory.py:14-23; add(2, 3) = 5); no network, no subprocess server
install_check.limits: Recipe install/import integration on the host network; no model request, image build or container acceptance

server_side_streamable_http.fastmcp: its own HTTP server (fastmcp/server/http.py builds a StreamableHTTPSessionManager), its event store and the FastMCP 1.x adapters

importer_review.recipe_use: Client only: the recipe's enabled MCP servers are stdio processes and its one HTTP entry, ai-memory, is disabled (config/mcp.template.json; host.py:361); the SDK's MCP code at fcc102a is client-side (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/mcp/client.py:1-8 on fastmcp's Client; the agent server's /mcp REST router, openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/mcp_router.py:29-56, calls configured servers), and a search of the four SDK packages finds no MCP server-side HTTP import. The recipe runs neither a fastmcp HTTP server nor the LiteLLM proxy
importer_review.limits: Static text search of single-line import statements in the relocked venv; not a runtime trace. The relock follows the scan finding, not a reachability finding
